2) Evidence attribution is sometimes inconsistent: in the supporting_chain step A (“torsion_access”), E71 (solid/film emission at 622 nm) is cited as an “aTB structural cue,” but E71 is not a structural cue; it is an observation. The structural cue is E31/E37 (and arguably E21). This mis-citation makes the chain look more supported than it is.
3) The writeup acknowledges that emission evidence is “solid-only” with “medium reliability” and no shift context (E72, E73), but still leans on an AIE-style restriction-of-motion story. With only a single solid emission point (E71), you cannot distinguish AIE from simply “only measured in solid,” nor can you validate a TICT-gated nonradiative channel in solution.

6) The electronic redistribution evidence is moderate (E36; and delta_gap moderately decreased in E22/E32), but the permanent dipole change is small and negative (E62), which weakens a strong CT/TICT argument. The current rationale does not reconcile why “CT-like family axis” is emphasized when dipole does not increase.

This is a mechanistic-definition conflict; if TICT remains top-1, it should be framed as “TICT-like neighbors but torsion coordinate tracked here does not capture the active twist,” or else downgraded toward ICT/neutral aromatic.

4) ESIPT plausibility mismatch: the structure motif profile says “intramolecular H-bond geometry is possible/likely” but “tautomerizable motif none” and “proton_transfer_local_geometry none” (structure_motif_profile; also aligned with E57 “proton_transfer_readiness_outlier low”).
